notable_absence.finding: This is the Capella tree's index hub page and it never states the two-class Traditional/Vector split that the registry promoted from server/'s indexes.md (index-class:traditional / index-class:vector), even though its own Index Commands section lists both traditional and vector DDL and its Related Links point at vector indexes. Nor does it name the Index Service anywhere in prose - the service appears only inside a link path (../clusters/index-service/manage-indexes.md) - so the page that fronts the Index Service documentation never says which service owns the thing it documents. Also absent: any definition of what an index is. The page has exactly one prose sentence (the abstract); everything else is a bullet list of links. No relation could be extracted for 'index-type:gsi providesIndexType' or 'dependsOnService' from this page for want of a sentence, and those omissions are absences of text, not of fact.

cross_component_finding: Two title/content mismatches, both load-bearing for this batch. (1) The page is titled 'Primary and Secondary Index Reference' and its abstract scopes it to primary and GSI indexes, yet its Index Commands list contains CREATE/ALTER/DROP VECTOR INDEX and its Related Links section points at 'Use Vector Indexes for AI Applications' - vector indexes are in the page's scope but not in its title. (2) The link labelled 'Index Storage Settings' targets storage-modes.md, whose own H1 is also 'Index Storage Settings'. Three names for one page - filename says 'modes', title and link text say 'settings' - and the page body (see the storage-modes.json record for this round) uses neither word: it says 'Index Storage' and 'standard index storage'. The registry's promoted ids index:standard-storage and index:memory-optimized-storage are glossed as 'storage mode', a word this Capella page never uses.
cross_product_finding: Capella files this hub at cloud/indexes/, a top-level directory named for a plural noun, whereas server/ files its equivalent under learn/services-and-indexes/indexes/ - i.e. beneath the service that owns it. That directory name is the documented origin of the retired `indexes:` namespace: the ids were minted from the folder rather than the subject. The Capella structure also splits what server/ keeps together: the 'Index Commands' listed here are all in cloud/n1ql/ while the conceptual pages are in cloud/indexes/, so a reader following this hub crosses trees on every second link.
